summary: This note is a Wikipedia-style overview of Golestan Province, one of Iran's 31 provinces in the north-east, south of the Caspian Sea. It covers the province's capital, its regional placement, its population and area, its administrative counties, and its history of separation from Mazandaran and renaming of Gorgan.
one_line: Overview of Golestan Province, a north-eastern Iranian province south of the Caspian Sea, with capital Gorgan and twelve counties.
key_facts: Golestān Province is one of the 31 provinces of Iran.
Golestān Province is located in the north-east of Iran, south of the Caspian Sea.
The capital of Golestān Province is Gorgan.
On June 22, 2014, the provinces were divided into 5 regions solely for coordination and development purposes, and Golestān Province was put as part of Region 1.
The majority of the population of Golestān Province are Sunni Muslims.
Golestān was split off from the province of Mazandaran in 1997.
Golestān Province has a population of 1.7 million (2011).
Golestān Province has an area of 20,380 km².
The province is divided into twelve counties (shahrestans).
The twelve counties of Golestān Province are Aliabad, Aqqala, Azadshahr, Bandar-e Gaz, Gonbad-e Qabus, Gorgan, Kalaleh, Kordkuy, Maraveh Tappeh, Minudasht, Ramian, and Torkaman.
Present-day Gorgan was called Esterabad until 1937.
